# PDFium – third-party licenses

Raffica uses the precompiled PDFium binaries from [bblanchon/pdfium-binaries](https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries) through the NuGet packages `bblanchon.PDFium.Win32` and `bblanchon.PDFium.Linux` (without V8, without XFA).

## Version

- NuGet packages: `160.0.8165` (see `Directory.Packages.props`)
- `VERSION` file of the release archives: `MAJOR=160`, `MINOR=0`, `BUILD=8165`, `PATCH=0`
- Release: `chromium/8165`

## Source

The NuGet packages themselves contain **no** license files (only binaries, import libraries, headers and a README). The licenses in this folder therefore come from the release archives of the same version:

| Archive | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases/download/chromium%2F8165/pdfium-win-x64.tgz` | `ca7338ae7779b8b1b82f4580305c4d762d214f8df1d54b47647fe3cc75989ded` |
| `https://github.com/bblanchon/pdfium-binaries/releases/download/chromium%2F8165/pdfium-linux-x64.tgz` | `ba7865e16c0271daab75256790be06c26272190afe6e2a70eae0bb39bb99089c` |

Taken over are the file `LICENSE` (license of Benoit Blanchon's build scripts, MIT) and the folder `licenses/` (PDFium itself and the libraries linked into it, such as FreeType, ICU, libjpeg-turbo, OpenJPEG, libpng, zlib, Little CMS, HarfBuzz, Abseil, Highway).

## Differences between the archives

Both archives contain the same files with the same content. They differ only in the line endings: in the Windows archive some files have CRLF (the `LICENSE` mixed CRLF/LF), in the Linux archive all have LF. The files were taken from the Linux archive, which matches the LF rule of the repository (`.gitattributes`). `licenses/freetype.txt` is ISO-8859-1 encoded in both archives and stays unchanged.

The nuspec of the NuGet packages names `Apache-2.0` as the license; the `LICENSE` of the archives is MIT. Both are compatible with GPL-3.0.

## Build arguments

From `args.gn` of both archives (relevant for Raffica):

```
pdf_enable_v8 = false
pdf_enable_xfa = false
```

So no JavaScript runs in PDFs, and XFA forms are not supported.

## Shipping

The license texts are part of `src/Raffica.Pdf/Resources/ThirdPartyNotices.txt` (generated by `dotnet run tools/licenses.cs -- generate` from `third-party/licenses.json`), which the app embeds for its About card and every package ships as `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`.

## Updating

The Windows and Linux packages must always move to the same version together (Dependabot groups them in one pull request). A PDFium bump also needs a refresh of the licenses in this folder from the new archives, of the version numbers above, and of the headers the native bindings are checked against (`NativeBindingsTests`).
